Article Title: HC pulls up UP govt over registration of FIRs under law declared 'stillborn' by SC
Article Text:
HC seeks explanation from UP govt over continued Gangsters Act FIRs despite SC declaring the law 'stillborn

HC flags failure to comply with SC ruling

NEW DELHI: The Allahabad high court's Lucknow Bench has sought an explanation from the Uttar Pradesh government over the continued registration of FIRs under the Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986, despite the Supreme Court having declared the law "stillborn" in August 2026.The court on Friday directed the additional chief secretary (Home) to submit a personal affidavit within three weeks explaining why cases were still being registered under the Act, news agency PTI reported.A division bench of Justices Abdul Moin and Pramod Kumar warned that if the affidavit is not filed, the officer would have to appear personally before the court along with the relevant records. The matter has been listed for December 15."Once the law with regard to the Act has been enunciated by the apex court in August 2026, there cannot be any occasion for the authorities to continue with the registration of FIRs under the provisions of the Act," PTI quoted the bench as saying.The court also sought details of the action proposed against officials responsible for registering such FIRs and the corrective measures being taken to prevent the recurrence of such cases.The bench remarked that it should not repeatedly have to point out the authorities' failure to comply with Supreme Court judgments. It also expressed concern that litigants were being compelled to approach the high court over the issue, leading to a waste of "precious judicial time of the Constitutional court".The observations came during the hearing of a writ petition filed by Brijesh Kumar alias Banty Verma, who challenged an FIR registered on October 23 under Section 3(1) of the Act at Akbarpur police station in Ambedkar Nagar district.The petitioner argued that the Supreme Court, in its August 2026 judgment in Shiv Pratap Singh alias Chinu vs State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, had declared the Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986, "stillborn". He contended that authorities could not continue proceedings under the legislation.Taking note of the submissions, the high court stayed the FIR and directed that no further proceedings be undertaken in the matter until further orders.The bench also noted that additional government advocates had earlier brought the continued registration of FIRs under the Act to the authorities' attention. However, apparently, no action had been taken to address the issue.The court has now sought an explanation from the state government on the continued registration of such cases and the steps being taken to ensure compliance with the Supreme Court's ruling.
Article Summary: HC seeks explanation from UP govt over continued Gangsters Act FIRs. SC declaring the law'stillborn' in August 2026. Allahabad high court's Lucknow Bench has sought an explanation from the Uttar Pradesh government over the continued registration of such cases.

Article Title: 'Nitish conceived the project': Prashant Kishor's rare praise for former Bihar CM with a jibe at BJP, RJD
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj chief said that the idea for the bridge was envisaged when Nitish was running a minority government.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Saturday praised former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar and credited him for the construction of the Raghopur-Bidupur bridge over the Ganga. Kishor also accused BJP and RJD of trying to claim credit for the newly built bridge.While talking to reporters, Jan Suraaj chief said that the idea for the bridge was envisaged between the 2014 Lok Sabha elections and 2015 assembly elections. During this period, Nitish was running a minority government."RJD often engages in such politics. I do not want to comment on that. If trains can be named after Modi, I don’t see any problem with naming a bridge after Nitish Kumar. Nobody in Bihar would object to it. There could be no denying that it was Kumar who conceived the project. Both the BJP and the RJD are unnecessarily trying to claim their share of credit," news agency PTI quotes Prashant Kishor as saying.Kishor also accused the Centre of neglecting Bihar and said that the state continues to lag behind other states on parameters such as per capita income, contribution to the national GDP, flood management, education and employment."As Modi arrives here, he should explain why, despite him being in office for 12 years at the Centre, Bihar, led by a double-engine government, continues to fall further behind other states in terms of per capita income, GDP, education, employment, etc.," he said.His remarks came as Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Vaishali district and inaugurated the bridge, named Nitish Setu after the former CM.Kishor also said that it would have been a greater tribute to Nitish if the government sincerely implemented the programmes he had initiated under the Saat Nishchay programme instead of merely naming a bridge after him.Responding to allegations that Nitish was underrepresented in NDA posters vis-à-vis senior BJP leaders ahead of the bridge’s inauguration, Kishor said the BJP was gradually swallowing JD(U) politically."Amit Shah runs the JD(U) today. He will naturally seek to promote the BJP's flag and give greater prominence to Modi’s face. Why would he promote Nitish Kumar?” he said."Despite the JD(U) having almost an equal number of MLAs as the BJP, neither Kumar nor his party appears to have any role in the functioning of the government, its publicity or its political communication. Even during the Chhath festival, there were posters of Modi and Samrat Choudhary, but not Kumar," he added.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor praised former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar and credited him for the construction of the Raghopur-Bidupur bridge over the Ganga. He accused BJP and RJD of trying to claim credit for the newly built bridge. His remarks came as Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Vaishali district and inaugurated the bridge.

Article Title: 'Voice of every village': Rahul attacks BJP after Congress's Rajasthan panchayat poll gains
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday hailed the party's performance in Rajasthan's panchayat elections, taking a swipe at the BJP saying the results reflected "the voice of every village" in the country.Sharing a post on X, Rahul thanked voters in rural Rajasthan for placing their trust in Congress, saying the mandate had become the party's responsibility."Heartfelt thanks to our brothers and sisters in rural Rajasthan. The trust you have placed in Congress in the panchayat elections is now our responsibility," he said.Rahul alleged that the results were a direct response to the BJP's "double engine" government, accusing the ruling party of weakening MGNREGA , hurting farmers and stripping panchayats of their powers."The BJP attacked MGNREGA, pushed farmers into losses, and stripped panchayats of their powers. Inflation, unemployment, and migration have emptied the villages," he said."The villages were watching everything, enduring everything. Now they have spoken. This is not just Rajasthan's mandate, it is the voice of every village in the country," Rahul added.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the party's victory in the Panchayati Raj elections showed that people were determined to hold the BJP accountable for its "double-engine misrule"."From Rajasthan to other states across the country, people are looking to Congress with hope and trust. Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan. Warm congratulations to all the dedicated leaders and hardworking workers of @INCRajasthan, who came together to raise grassroots issues and strengthen the people's trust," he said in a Hindi post on X.Kharge said the trust placed in the party by voters was its greatest responsibility.Meanwhile, the BJP state president accepted defeat and said that party respected the people's mandate and would introspect on its performance following the results."Today, the election results for various Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis across Rajasthan have been announced. We accept the public mandate" Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore said.“We will also review where we may have faltered; we will examine these aspects and remain, as always, deeply committed to public service," he added.The results come as a setback to the BJP ahead of the Bhajanlal Sharma-led government's third anniversary in December, PTI reported.According to figures on the State Election Commission website on Friday evening, results were available for 7,393 of the 7,543 Panchayat Samiti seats and 981 of the 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 districts.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi hails the party's performance in Rajasthan's panchayat elections. He says the results reflected "the voice of every village" in the country. The BJP state president accepted defeat and said that party respected the people's mandate.

Article Title: ‘Local DCP suddenly on leave, new DCP in’: CJP's Dipke hints at jail time; Delhi Police detains protesters - top developments
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, along with Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das, National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and Singer Vishal Dadlani during a protest seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park.

Journalist Roshie detained: Neha

TMC extends support to CJP

'We follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi': Dipke

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: Girl gang-raped at party in Mumbai, FIR on woman, 3 others
Article Text:
(Representative) A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by two men in Kashigaon after a party invitation





MUMBAI: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by two men after being invited to a party by her female friend in Kashigaon on Nov 16. The accused allegedly forced her to consume alcohol before sexually assaulting her.Kashigaon police have registered a case against four people, including the friend, and are searching for all the accused.According to the complaint, the victim's 25-year-old friend Sheetal called her around 9pm and introduced her to three men - Piyush Thakur, Dushyant Singh and Ahat Khan. The group took her to Khan's flat in Vinay Nagar, where she was allegedly forced to consume alcohol.Sheetal and Piyush later went downstairs, leaving the girl with Khan and Dushyant, who allegedly took turns raping her between midnight and 6am. The victim also alleged that a five-gram gold chain was stolen from her neck.The incident came to light after she failed to return home, prompting her mother to make inquiries. Police have booked all four under relevant Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and POCSO Act provisions . All four are absconding, officials said.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by two men after being invited to a party by her female friend in Kashigaon. The accused allegedly forced her to consume alcohol before sexually assaulting her. Police have registered a case against four people, including the friend, and are searching for all the accused.

Article Title: Son of Delhi doctor accused of killing domestic help dies; father moves court for interim bail
Article Text:
In photos: The accused Dr Manish Gupta; the victim domestic help





NEW DELHI: Dr Manish Gupta, an accused in the domestic help murder case, has approached a Delhi court seeking three weeks' interim bail following the death of his 19-year-old son, Parth Gupta, on November 19.Gupta has sought temporary release to attend his son's last rites and be with his family during the bereavement. He is currently in judicial custody after being arrested by Delhi Police on June 18, 2026, and is facing trial in the murder case before Saket District Court.Additional Sessions Judge Anuj Aggarwal took note of the application and directed Delhi Police to submit a verification report. The court has listed the matter for hearing on Saturday.Moving the application on Gupta's behalf, advocate Kamal Nayan Tiwari submitted that the accused was facing an extremely difficult situation following the sudden death of his only child. He argued that Gupta, as the deceased's father, had an emotional and moral responsibility to attend the last rites, but his continued custody had prevented him from doing so.The counsel told the court that he received a call from Gupta's wife on November 20, informing him that their 19-year-old son had died a day earlier. The application stated that the death had come as a devastating shock to the family and that Gupta was unable to be present with them because he was in custody.Parth was also named as a suspect in the charge sheet filed by Delhi Police in the domestic help murder case and had been questioned during the investigation.
Article Summary: Dr Manish Gupta, an accused in the domestic help murder case, has approached a Delhi court seeking three weeks' interim bail. His 19-year-old son, Parth Gupta, died on November 19. Gupta is currently in judicial custody after being arrested by Delhi Police on June 18, 2026.

Article Title: Rajasthan Congress chief demands CM Sharma resign over panchayat poll setback
Article Text:
PCC Chief Govind dotasara and LoP Tikaram Jully with Party workers Celebrate Panchayati Raj election results Friday





JAIPUR: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra Friday demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and his cabinet, terming BJP’s setback in panchayat elections as “public anger” over alleged corruption, administrative lapses and unfulfilled promises.Addressing a news conference at the Congress office in Jaipur, Dotasra said the state govt was focused on optics rather than governance. “The state govt appears more interested in publicity and ceremonial events than addressing people’s problems,” he said.Taking aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s earlier description of BJP’s urban local body performance as a “landslide victory,” Dotasra argued the results did not support the claim. He said BJP’s lead over Congress was marginal and claimed that “nearly 64% of voters voted against it” in the urban polls.“People have exposed the PM’s claim (in rural polls). Modi should be wary of the ‘facts’ fed to him by Rajasthan BJP, which only ends up embarrassing him,” Dotasra said.He reiterated his demand for resignations, saying, “If the CM and his ministers have even a little moral responsibility left, they should resign and tell the PM and the Union home minister that they have failed to meet the expectations of Rajasthan’s people.”Dotasra alleged the Sharma govt failed to address inflation, healthcare, fertiliser and seed availability for farmers, employment and women’s safety. Referring to alleged irregularities in medicines and medical equipment supplied to pregnant women, he accused the govt of evading accountability for maternal deaths. He also alleged that job seekers were facing police action. Unemployed youth, he said, were being met with “batons and police action instead of recruitment opportunities. ”Dotasra also criticised Sharma over remarks directed at former chief minister Ashok Gehlot , saying Gehlot’s advice to keep relatives away from govt affairs stemmed from his experience as a three-term CM. “Instead of addressing the issue, the current CM appears rattled. The language he used against a former CM was unacceptable. Even a street drunkard would not use such language,” Dotasra said.Questioning Sharma’s emphasis on high-profile visits and public events, Dotasra took a swipe at the ceremonial aspects of VIP tours. “A ‘Radhe Radhe’ stole, a memento, a helicopter ride and visits by the PM and the Union HM—but what did Rajasthan’s people get? You are not running an event management company; you are running a govt,” he said.
Article Summary: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra Friday demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and his cabinet. He terming BJP’s setback in panchayat elections as “public anger” over alleged corruption, administrative lapses and unfulfilled promises.

Article Title: Ashok Chavan criticises Rohit Pawar for targeting Fadnavis
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





BJP MP and former Maharashtra chief minister Ashok Chavan on Thursday hit out at NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar over his allegations against chief minister Devendra Fadnavis in connection with the plane crash that killed deputy CM Ajit Pawar .Calling Pawar’s allegations “baseless”, Chavan questioned his political intent. “It appears Rohit Pawar is in a hurry to establish himself as a political leader,” Chavan told reporters in Nanded .Pawar had accused Fadnavis of shielding the airline involved in the crash. Chavan rejected the charge.In a separate political departure from his party’s stand, Chavan said he would read Congress politician Sonia Gandhi ’s autobiography, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, despite BJP opposing the book.Chavan, who spent more than four decades in Congress before joining BJP, said his long association with the party made him curious about Gandhi’s account.“I was in Congress for several years, so I should know what happened during that period,” he said.“Sonia Gandhi has witnessed several ups and downs in her political and personal life, and the book recounts those experiences. There is nothing beyond that,” he said.Asked about BJP protests in which copies of the book were torn, Chavan struck a cautious note. He said everyone had their own perspective and took positions accordingly, but declined to comment further.BJP has accused Gandhi of using the autobiography to gloss over mistakes made during Congress govts. Party workers have protested against the book at several places.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra chief minister Ashok Chavan hit out at NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar over his allegations against chief minister Devendra Fadnavis. Chavan questioned Pawar’s political intent, saying he was in a hurry to establish himself as a political leader. In a separate political departure from his party's stand, Chavan said he would read Congress politician Sonia Gandhi ’s autobiography.

Article Title: Farmers stage road blockade in Beed
Article Text:
Farmers during their protest outside Chousala bus stand in Beed taluka on Thursday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Farmers staged a road blockade outside the Chousala bus stand on Thursday, protesting alleged harassment, financial exploitation and intimidation by wind energy companies operating in the Balaghat hill range in Beed taluka. The protesters alleged that farmers opposing the companies’ activities were being threatened with extortion cases to silence them.The farmers alleged that wind energy companies were installing electricity poles and laying transmission lines through agricultural land without obtaining the consent of landowners. They also accused the companies of denying farmers adequate compensation and, in some cases, issuing cheques that could not be encashed, thereby causing financial losses.Organised by the Shetkari Hakka Morcha, the agitation saw farmers from Chousala, Kanadighat, Golangri, Malewadi, Borkhed, Ghargaon, Ruigavhan, Wadwadi and Babhalgaon express anger against the functioning of windmill companies in their areas.They raised slogans demanding an end to alleged high-handedness and exploitation by the companies and condemning the revenue and police administrations for allegedly protecting them.The farmers further alleged that those opposing such work were subjected to threats and intimidation, including threats of being booked in extortion cases. They also claimed that land acquisition activities were being carried out illegally with the alleged connivance of certain officials from the revenue and police departments.After the protest, the farmers submitted a memorandum through the district collector to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and guardian minister Sunetra Pawar.Beed tehsildar Chandrakant Shelke and Neknoor police station assistant inspector Mangesh Salve received the memorandum. Police sub-inspectors and personnel from Neknoor police station were also present.Ganesh Dhawale, who raised the issue during the agitation, said the state industries, energy and labour department had issued a govt resolution on Oct 21, 2013, providing for district, taluka and sub-divisional monitoring committees for wind energy projects.“Despite the committees being constituted, their functioning is not effective. Farmers have repeatedly approached the administration with complaints but have failed to get justice. This has emboldened the companies to continue their alleged exploitation and harassment,” Dhawale said.
Article Summary: Farmers staged a road blockade outside the Chousala bus stand in Beed taluka. They are protesting alleged harassment, financial exploitation and intimidation by wind energy companies operating in the Balaghat hill range. The protesters alleged that farmers opposing the companies’ activities were being threatened with extortion cases to silence them.

Article Title: 50-year-old man accused of spiking woman's drink, raping her at Belapur lodge

NAVI MUMBAI: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist.Dwivedi was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha and four others of Rs 19 lakh in a flat sale deal. He is currently lodged in Taloja jail.Senior inspector Arun Pawar of CBD-Belapur police station said the woman alleged that on May 30 last year, she had attended a birthday party at Arush Hotel in Sector 15, CBD-Belapur, and was also there to collect Rs 10,000 from Jha. Dwivedi, who was present at the party, allegedly spiked her soft drink. After she felt dizzy, he took her to Arush Lodge and sexually assaulted her.She further alleged that Dwivedi threatened to kill her and her family if she disclosed the incident to anyone. He also threatened to circulate an intimate video, which he had allegedly recorded on his mobile phone.Pawar said, "The woman claimed that she did not approach the police earlier because of Dwivedi's threats.After learning that he had been arrested in another case and lodged in jail, she came forward and registered an FIR against him."Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to rape, administering stupefying or intoxicating substances, aggravated criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of public peace.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme Court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist. He was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha. He is currently lodged in Taloja jail.

Article Title: AITA interim body has ‘ceased to exist’ in HC-approved form: Administrator Mittal
Article Text: Pune: In a significant development that puts a question mark on the AITA election process, the federation’s court-appointed Administrator Justice (Retd.) Gita Mittal has told the Delhi High Court that the Interim Executive Committee (IEC) has “ceased to exist” in its court-approved form following Dinesh Arora’s resignation as treasurer and his replacement without her approval.In an application filed on Friday, the Administrator has alleged that the IEC had no authority to assign the Treasurer’s responsibilities to Sudarshan Ghosh, who had neither contested nor been declared elected to the post.She has also accused the IEC of effectively ousting her from AITA’s election process and independently assuming functions that she says the court had entrusted to her.These allegedly include appointment of the Electoral Officer, issuance of the election notification and processes relating to women representatives, Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit and the Athletes Committee.The Administrator has further alleged that financial transactions were conducted without her prior approval or knowledge and that information required to prepare the electoral college was not provided to her.The application follows the High Court’s November 6 order recording AITA’s undertaking that the Administrator would continue until completion of the elections and that information sought by her would continue to be provided.The court had directed AITA to remain bound by the undertaking.The Administrator has asked the court to take cognisance of the alleged illegalities and “usurpation” of authority by the IEC and reaffirm that all election-related steps must emanate from and remain under her superintendence, rather than being undertaken independently by the interim body or its members.She has also sought any further directions considered appropriate by the court.The court has posted the latest application from the Administrator for hearing on November 27, the day of the AITA elections. However, the Administrator’s legal team is most likely to move the court on Monday for an urgent hearing.
Article Summary: Court-appointed Administrator Justice (Retd.) Gita Mittal has told the Delhi High Court that the Interim Executive Committee (IEC) has “ceased to exist” in its court-approved form. She has accused the IEC of effectively ousting her from AITA’s election process and independently assuming functions that she says the court had entrusted to her.

Article Title: Woman bludgeoned to death by brother-in-law after being hit by mini-truck near Saswad
Article Text:
Pune:





Pune Rural police on Thursday arrested a 51-year-old mini-truck driver from Bibvewadi for allegedly bludgeoning his 47-year-old sister-in-law to death.The murder took place around 9 am on Thursday at Pandare village near Saswad, about 42 km from Pune, when the victim, Ujjwala Kakade, was walking to catch a bus to Hadapsar. Kakade worked as a teacher at a private school in Hadapsar.A Saswad police team led by inspector Santosh Gholave arrested the accused, Shashikant Kakade, who had fled the spot. Shashikant and his mother have been booked under Section 103 (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Gholave said the victim’s husband died about six months ago following a prolonged illness. After his brother’s death, the accused took away the victim’s money, gold jewellery, a piece of land and other important documents. “The victim was pursuing the accused for them. They had a dispute over it,” Gholave said.Assistant police inspector Vaibhav Sonawane of the Saswad police said when the woman was on her way to school on Thursday morning, the accused rammed his mini-truck into her. After she fell to the ground, he bludgeoned her to death with an iron rod and bricks. “The accused had fled from the spot. We arrested him in the evening,” Sonawane said. He said the victim’s brother, who is the complainant, alleged that his sister’s mother-in-law was also involved in the murder. “We have registered the case against her as well. Our investigation is under way,” he said.
Article Summary: The murder took place around 9 am on Thursday at Pandare village near Saswad, about 42 km from Pune. The victim, Ujjwala Kakade, was walking to catch a bus to Hadapsar. Shashikant Kakade and his mother have been booked under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Article Title: Congress demands FIR, independent probe into Bhusawal voter objections
Article Text:
Harshwardhan Sapkal

Nashik:





A total of 183 people filed objections against the names of 14,567 electors in the Bhusawal assembly constituency in Jalgaon district, prompting the district election office to verify the claims.However, the Congress has questioned the process irrespective of its outcome, demanding an FIR and a thorough inquiry into who filed the objections and how bulk applications were permitted in an alleged attempt to delete eligible voters.While the district election office stated that verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) found all entries genuine except those of 74 deceased electors, Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded strict action against those involved.“The state Election Commission has been urged to order an independent inquiry into this matter, immediately register an FIR, and take strict action against all those responsible, including the masterminds behind it. No attempt to deprive voters of their rights will be tolerated,” Sapkal wrote in a post on X.The Congress has alleged that the objections were filed in a coordinated manner, with some applications submitted in the names of people who later denied filing them. It has sought an independent, time-bound inquiry by officials from outside Jalgaon district, along with action against those responsible for preparing and accepting the applicationsCongress city president Ahmed Qureshi and party members objected to the Form-7 claims raised by the 183 unverified citizens before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Bhusawal.“We are unable to understand how 183 applicants raised objections to 14,567 names in a single day when an individual can file only 10 applications. This is a perfect example showing that BJP people are trying their ways and means to delete the names of people who are not in their favour,” claimed Qureshi.Congress district president Dhananjay Chaudhari said party workers met some applicants who were unaware of objections filed in their names. “The people against whom objections were filed were genuine as claimed by the administration. However, this does not solve our issue. The administration should conduct a thorough inquiry to find out who filed the objections using CCTV footage, and file an FIR against them,” demanded Chaudhari, warning of strong agitation in the event of failure.Electoral registration officer Jitendra Patil said, “The objections were filed through ‘inward’ in the office and hence had to be attended to as per Election Commission of India norms. Booth Level Officers thoroughly checked them, and we found only 74 names of electors who had died some time back. All other names are safe.”
Article Summary: A total of 183 people filed objections against the names of 14,567 electors in the Bhusawal assembly constituency in Jalgaon district. The district election office stated that verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) found all entries genuine except those of 74 deceased electors. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded strict action against those involved.

COIMBATORE: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has permanently removed Prakash , the party’s Vadavalli town secretary, from his post and all party responsibilities following a video of him creating a ruckus inside a two-wheeler showroom circulated on social media.The announcement stated that the action was taken following a video circulated in the media and complaints from party functionaries.The party said Prakash had allegedly acted in a manner contrary to its policies, objectives and principles, bringing disrepute to the organisation.The order, signed by V Raghukumar, Coimbatore North district secretary of TVK, said Prakash had been removed permanently from all party posts and even the primary membership to maintain discipline within the organisation.Earlier, a video of him making a ruckus inside a two-wheeler showroom near Vadavalli in the city was circulated on social media.In the video, a woman was alleging that Prakash received a bribe to give her a party posting. She also alleged that he made derogatory comments about her.Vadavalli police have registered two separate cases against Prakash and Dhivya and are investigating.

Article Title: Rash and wrong-side driving: Coimbatore district police book driver, seize private bus, recommend cancellation of licence and permit
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore district police have seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving at Pappampatti Pirivu on the Coimbatore–Palladam Road.According to a statement issued by the district police on Tuesday, the incident occurred around 8.30am on Monday while the private bus was heading to Coimbatore from Tirupur. Near Pappampatti Pirivu, which falls under the Sulur police station limits, driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic on the wrong side of the busy stretch, putting motorists and pedestrians at a grave risk.Several commuters recorded the dangerous manoeuvre and uploaded the footage online, where it quickly gained widespread traction. Acting on a formal complaint lodged by a motorist, the Sulur police registered a case against Sakthivel under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) read with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act Police impounded the bus and parked it on the Sulur police station premises for further legal proceedings. Additionally, authorities have written to the regional transport officer recommending the cancellation of Sakthivel’s driving licence as well as the vehicle’s route permit.Reiterating a zero-tolerance stance, the district police warned that strict legal action would be taken against motorists endangering public safety.
Article Summary: The Coimbatore district police seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving. Driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic.

Article Title: Verdict on Sulur minor girl rape-murder case postponed to Nov 27
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A special court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases on Monday postponed to Nov 27 its verdict on the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl near Sulur in Coimbatore district.The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement.On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayam lakebed. Police arrested K Karthi,35, and R Mohan, 31, both of whom were residing in the same locality.Police registered a case under sections 5(m), 5(i), 6(1), 5(I), 5(j)(iv), 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act and 103(1), 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4), 238(a), 127(2), 65, 49, 240, 249(a) of the BNS. The first hearing of the case took place on June 10. Prime accused Karthi was lodged in Madurai Central Prison, while Mohan was lodged in Trichy Central Prison.On Monday, both were produced before the court. While police were bringing them to the court, Mohan asked the media people not to take video of him, claiming that police had falsely included him in the case.
Article Summary: The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement. On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayan lakebed.

Article Title: Man arrested with leopard claws in Sathyamangalam
Article Text:
Police are investigating to trace how it came in his possession

Erode

:





A 54-year-old man was arrested by forest protection squad officials for possessing leopard claws near Sathyamangalam on Saturday evening.He was apprehended when a special team conducted a patrol along the Sathyamangalam–Athani Road, following a tip-off. During the operation, officials noticed a man standing alone under suspicious circumstances near the Hospital Medu bus stop. “A subsequent search of the suspect led to the recovery of two leopard claws,” said a forest officer.The man was identified as Shanmugam, 54, of Kuttai Thottam, in Sathyamangalam taluk. He was taken to the Sathyamangalam forest range office for further interrogation.A wildlife offense case was subsequently registered against him. The accused and the seized claws were produced before the judicial magistrate in Sathyamangalam on Saturday night. Further investigation is on.
Article Summary: A 54-year-old man was arrested by forest protection squad officials for possessing leopard claws. He was apprehended when a special team conducted a patrol along the Sathyamangalam–Athani Road, following a tip-off. Police are investigating to trace how it came in his possession.

A man was arrested on Thursday for allegedly attacking a woman with scissors after she opposed his alleged pressure to convert and plan to marry another woman. He subsequently fled.Acting station house officer Ashish Chaubey said police registered a case under relevant sections based on the woman’s written complaint.During questioning, the accused admitted that he was attempting to flee to Noida. He was produced before a court and sent to jail.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: HC summons three IAS officers in bogus library books scam
Article Text:
HC summons three IAS officers in bogus library books scam

Madurai

:





People at the helm of affairs are bound to answer, observed the Madras high court on Friday, while issuing statutory notices summoning three IAS officers to appear before the court and seeking their explanation in connection with the bogus library books purchase scam.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice M D Sumathi issued the statutory notices to former director of public libraries Jayanthi , former school education department secretary Chandramohan and former managing director of Tamil Nadu textbook and educational services corporation Aarthi.The judges directed the state govt to place before the court the relevant files regarding the procurement of books for public libraries.During the course of the hearing, the state submitted that suggestions collected by the court would be placed for consideration and would be deliberated upon. A comprehensive policy regarding the procurement of books for public libraries would also be issued in eight weeks. The proposed policy would plug all loopholes that had now surfaced, the state submitted.Taking into account that a similar case was pending before the principal seat in Chennai and considering the special facts and circumstances of the case, the judges requested Justice V Lakshminarayanan, holding the roster (V and AC cases) at the principal seat, to monitor the investigation conducted by the DVAC in the scam.During the previous hearing, the court observed, “The government would do well to undertake a detailed probe and come out with a statement as to how procurement of books had taken place for the last 20 years and more. It would be in order if a ‘White paper’ was submitted. The scam had shaken the conscience of the people of Tamil Nadu. Their faith in the system must be restored.”The state submitted that five officials had already been suspended.The court was hearing the contempt petition filed by V Ramasubbu complaining about the non-compliance with the earlier order passed by the court in 2024.
Article Summary: Madras high court summons three IAS officers in bogus library books scam. The judges directed the state govt to place before the court the relevant files regarding the procurement of books for public libraries. The court was hearing the contempt petition filed by V Ramasubbu.

Article Title: Central crime branch probes illegal quarrying cases, searches TN former minister P Moorthy's house
Article Text:
TN former minister P Moorthy





MADURAI: Madurai district police conducted a search on Friday at the residence of former minister P Moorthy in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying involving the extraction of minerals beyond permitted limits, causing substantial losses to the government.According to officials, a quarry lessee at Sathiravellalapatti in Vadipatti taluk allegedly excavated gravel stones beyond the sanctioned quantity and from land for which no permission had been obtained. Based on inspections conducted by the Department of Geology and Mining, the Revenue Divisional Officer reported that the alleged violations resulted in losses of Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore to the government in two separate instances.Acting on the complaints, the Madurai District Central Crime Branch registered two cases.As part of the investigation, a police team searched Moorthy's residence on Roja Street in Ezhil Nagar, Iyer Bungalow, after informing the Judicial Magistrate Court.Officials said the search was aimed at identifying documents and other materials related to the alleged illegal quarrying activities. Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Madurai district police conducted a search on Friday at the residence of former minister P Moorthy in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying. The alleged violations resulted in losses of Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore to the government in two separate instances.

Article Title: Tonsure fraud: DVAC books temple official, trustees’ chief
Article Text:
Tonsure fraud: DVAC books temple official, trustees’ chief





Madurai: Directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against 10 people, including the assistant commissioner and hereditary trustees’ chairman of Irukkankudi Mariamman temple near Sattur, for an alleged fraud in the free tonsure scheme.A surprise inspection on Nov 17 uncovered an alleged racket involving unauthorised barbers, compulsory collections from devotees and fabricated records to claim govt payments.Those booked include assistant commissioner Ilangovan, hereditary trustees’ chairman M Ramamoorthy, temple guard Singaravelu, office assistant Ganesan, assistant guard-cum-barber Yogarajan and five others.Investigators found that six officially appointed barbers had engaged 28 unauthorised workers to perform tonsures while continuing to receive payments from the temple administration. The workers were allegedly paid daily wages from money collected from devotees instead of being given regular salaries. Under the govt scheme, barbers receive ₹30 for each tonsure, while devotees are entitled to the service free of charge.DVAC also uncovered suspected manipulation of records to claim payments for tonsures never performed. Officials found 55 pre-printed tokens at the counter without corresponding devotees.Tokens were also issued without photographs, violating HR&CE department procedures.During the inspection, officials seized ₹59,520 in unaccounted cash from unauthorised barbers and ₹20,500 from a temple guard. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud, dating back to 2022, could involve several crores of rupees. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A surprise inspection on Nov 17 uncovered an alleged racket involving unauthorised barbers, compulsory collections from devotees and fabricated records. Under the govt scheme, barbers receive ₹30 for each tonsure, while devotees are entitled to the service free of charge. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud, dating back to 2022, could involve several crores of rupees.

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district. He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’

Article Title: 'First violence, now poisonous liquor': Rahul Gandhi accuses Manipur BJP govt of negligence over spurious alcohol deaths
Article Text:
Manipur chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Imphal's Shija Hospital to meet those hospitalised (PTI)

Methanol poisoning suspected

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday blamed the BJP-led Manipur government for what he described as negligence after at least 15 people died and around 150 were hospitalised following the suspected consumption of spurious liquor in Chandel district since November 18."This is not an accident but the result of negligence by the BJP government. First, violence destroyed hundreds of homes; now, poisonous liquor is devastating families, while the government continues to remain asleep," he said in a Hindi post on X, referring to the ethnic conflict that has gripped the northeastern state since 2023.The Lok Sabha leader of the opposition called for immediate action against those responsible and adequate compensation for the affected families."The news of several deaths due to spurious liquor in Manipur is deeply distressing. I extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish those undergoing treatment a speedy recovery," he added.Meanwhile, several patients admitted to Shija Hospitals and Research Institute in Imphal after allegedly consuming spurious liquor have shown symptoms consistent with methanol poisoning, raising suspicions that the locally made alcohol may have been contaminated with the toxic substance.Most of those affected are residents of Chakpikarong and adjoining areas of Chandel district.The hospital continues to receive patients requiring emergency medical care.Chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited the hospital to assess the situation and meet patients and medical teams.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi blamed the BJP-led Manipur government for what he described as negligence. At least 15 people died and around 150 were hospitalised following the suspected consumption of spurious liquor in Chandel district since November 18. Chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited the hospital to assess the situation and meet patients and medical teams.
